hold_text: Tier-2: two files under src/ (src/prop/prop_status_request.py, src/runtime/silent_refusal_alert.py). Neither changes an order decision — no sizing, no routing, no gate, no threshold. What changes is (a) which CAUSE NAME an already-existing operator alert prints, and (b) whether a suppression decision leaves a durable trace. WHAT A HUMAN SHOULD CHECK, in order of consequence: (1) THE CADENCE-FILE SHAPE CHANGED and the live VM holds the OLD shape right now — runtime_logs/prop_status_request.json currently reads {"breakout_1": "2026-09-09T07:47:07.098843+00:00"}, a bare string. `last_request_iso` accepts both; if it did not, every account would read as never-asked on the first tick after deploy and the whole fleet would be re-asked, silently resetting the cooldown MI-214 exists to bound. Two tests pin this (one unit, one end-to-end with a real legacy file) and a mutation that drops the string branch fails both. This is the half most worth a second pair of eyes. (2) THE QUIESCENT PATH MUST NOT STAMP `last_request` — it records `last_verdict` and leaves `last_request` as it was. If it stamped both, every tick would restart the 12h cooldown and a genuine ask would be suppressed forever. Mutation-tested. (3) The cause-rule ORDERING is the actual fix in silent_refusal_alert: the journalled reason contains BOTH `sizing_failed` and `prop_balance_stale`, and classify_cause returns the FIRST match, so the new rule must precede the generic one. A test asserts the index ordering directly rather than only the outcome, because a reorder would otherwise re-collapse the two silently. ⚠️ I did NOT add a CAUSE_MIN_ROWS override for the new cause, and a test asserts its ABSENCE with the reasoning: the balance_unreadable precedent was justified by MEASURED run lengths over 11 occurrences, whereas this event has never occurred even once, so there is nothing to size a lowered floor from. Lowering a bar on precedent alone is what canon forbids. If you would rather it alerted on a single occurrence, that is a one-line change and a legitimate call — but it should be yours, not mine.
why: MI-214b. TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN WORK, both measured rather than reasoned, and the first is why this PR is much smaller than the one the operator authorised. || (1) I FILED A BACKLOG ROW TODAY THAT WAS WRONG, AND IT IS CORRECTED IN PLACE RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED. BL-20260909-PROP-SIZING-REFUSAL-ON-A-STALE-BALANCE-IS-JOURNALED-BUT-NEVER-PINGED claimed a prop account blocked by a stale balance 'stops trading with NO operator-facing signal' and cited 4 journal rows as evidence. Re-read 2026-09-09T11:3xZ from /api/diag/journal?table=trades&limit=1000: those 4 rows are `balance() returned None` on ib_paper, alpaca_paper and alpaca_portfolio — the NON-prop branch, a different cause on different accounts. I had matched 'prop_balance' OR 'sizing_failed' over a json.dumps of each row and reported the union as if it were the first disjunct, over the WRONG TABLE (order_packages, not trades). breakout_1 has ZERO rows in that window and ZERO rows anywhere contain 'prop_balance' — the prop refusal has NEVER FIRED AT ALL. And 'reaches nobody' is false: log_rejection_to_journal -> _log_trade_to_journal writes to `trades`, which is exactly what silent_refusal_alert._read_window reads. I established that by RUNNING the real code (classify_cause and assess over the genuine string built from prop_balance.refusal_message), not by reading it — which is also how I avoided building a mechanism that already existed. What survives is narrower and real: the refusal matched the GENERIC `sizing_failed` rule, so the operator would be told the size computation failed when the actionable fact is 'send a fresh bal'. That is UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A, and per canon the remedy is to branch on the actual condition rather than reword a label. || (2) MI-214 (#11530, merged ffd13fa2, deployed b0dd0d67) SHIPPED ITS QUIESCENT VERDICT AT DEBUG, so the one verdict that SUPPRESSES the ask left no trace. MEASURED on the live VM minutes after it deployed: /api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-trader-live&lines=400 contained ZERO `prop_status_request` mentions while the tick was demonstrably alive (24 heartbeat mentions). 'The module ran and correctly stayed quiet' was therefore indistinguishable from 'it crashed on import' and from 'it never ran' — the collapsed-state failure this repo names, in the instrument rather than the data — and it BLOCKS MI-214's own done_condition (3), which requires an observation with a positive control. The verdict is now recorded durably in the cadence file, which ALREADY has a read surface (/api/diag/log_file?name=prop_status_request), rather than in a new file nothing is allowlisted to read (BL-20260825-ALERT-AND-CADENCE-STATE-FILES-SHIP-WITHOUT-A-READ-SURFACE). A journal line alone is NOT sufficient and that is stated rather than assumed: this branch is reached at most once per 12h cooldown and journald retention on this VM was measured at ~30 minutes, so the line is gone before anyone looks. || SCOPE: these are one concern — making the prop path's decisions visible to the operator — and splitting them would cost two ~19-minute CI cycles on a branch that re-conflicts every ~7 minutes for no reviewer benefit. || VALIDATION: 32 + 47 tests pass. FOUR mutants, each caught: drop the legacy-string branch (2 fail), stamp last_request on quiescent (1), reorder the cause rules (3), widen the new regex to swallow the generic bucket (1). Full guard set run in its own command after committing.
